note: A CLEAN TEXT MERGE OF AN AGGREGATE ARTIFACT IS UNRELIABLE NON-DETERMINISTICALLY ACROSS MERGE ORDERS, AND A WHOLE CRATE CAN VANISH FROM A DEFAULT-DENY AUDIT WITH NO CONFLICT MARKER. Measured today on docs/audits/type-audit-report.md, three times, twice with both sides of the evidence in hand. The file is an AGGREGATE -- counts by class and by crate, no per-symbol rows -- so a three-way merge of it is a valid merge of neither side. THE NEW PART: the merge queue on lefford and I independently merged THE SAME TWO COMMITS and got OPPOSITE resolutions of the same file. Its merge took mains values and silently dropped campaign/the-deeds six added primitives (language +5, vessel +1). Mine took the branchs values and silently dropped mains entire sentiment crate row, six items, a whole crate gone from an audit whose entire job is default-deny. Both merges were clean. Neither conflicted. Regeneration converged them on the same truth from opposite starting points, and the arithmetic closes both ways: from my side it added exactly sentiments 6 (flag +1, identifier-text +1, ratio +4), from theirs exactly the Deeds 6 (flag +2, identifier-text +2, prose +2). Earlier the same day the same file lost four counts to a clean merge while I absorbed 38 commits of main. CONSEQUENCE: never infer freshness of an aggregate from a clean merge, and do not treat an empty diff on one as evidence -- a clean-and-wrong merge and a correct one are indistinguishable until something regenerates. ALWAYS make rebaseline after an absorption and diff the paths docs/generated-paths.txt declares. HOW TO ATTRIBUTE A MOVED COUNT WITHOUT GUESSING, since the report has no per-symbol rows: the artifact is committed at every step, so walk it. git show COMMIT:docs/audits/type-audit-report.md piped to grep for the crate rows, once per task boundary, gives an exact per-commit attribution. That is what showed The Deeds six belonged to Tasks 2 and 4 and that Task 6 added zero -- diffing the report at the pre-task commit against the tip returned IDENTICAL, which is the cheapest possible answer to did this task tag something it should not have.
